reason: The hypothesis cites no prior evidence, and all key premises—from the effect of heat treatment on interface coherency to the specific dislocation-pile-up mechanism improving creep resistance—are specific claims requiring experimental support that is entirely absent.
premises: Post-deposition heat treatment can enhance coherency at FCC/BCC phase interfaces in high-entropy alloys.
Enhanced interface coherency increases the barrier to dislocation motion.
Increased barrier to dislocation motion promotes dislocation pile-ups at phase boundaries.
Dislocation pile-ups at reinforced boundaries distribute stress and raise the threshold for creep deformation.
This mechanism leads to reduced creep rate and higher stress threshold for creep initiation.
